summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ , a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and a history of recurrent urinary tract infections, was admitted with fatigue, fever, and shortness of breath after injuring his urethra during self-catheterization. He developed septic shock and acute kidney injury, with blood and urine cultures positive for ESBL-producing E. coli. He was treated in the ICU with vasopressors, fluid resuscitation, and initial vancomycin and Zosyn, then transitioned to meropenem. His condition improved, and he was transferred to the floor. A midline catheter was placed for continued IV antibiotics. His renal function normalized, and blood cultures cleared. Pressure ulcers on the hip and lower back were monitored and remained superficial. He was discharged to extended care to complete his antibiotic course, with plans to restart methenamine hippurate and resume self-catheterization with his preferred catheters.
